title: Memory is defined functionally as future behaviour modulated by past experience

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Memory is defined functionally as future behaviour modulated by past experience

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the basal cognition framework adopted by Biswas, Clawson and Levin, memory is defined in substrate-independent functionalist terms: a system has memory when its future behaviour is specifically modulated by its past experience, which allows the question of whether molecular networks such as gene regulatory networks are trainable.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 1. Introduction

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Consistent with the basal cognition paradigm, we define memory in functionalist terms—a system in which future behavior is specifically modulated by past experience.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “1. Introduction”. Scope: Any system, including gene regulatory networks and protein pathways

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-04: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.19

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The statement defines memory rather than asserting a contingent regularity. Its usefulness can be debated or applied, but no dataset can confirm or refute the definition itself.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: This is a stipulated functional definition; observations can determine whether a system satisfies it but cannot empirically confirm that this is the correct meaning of memory.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Competing definitions of memory are not distinguished by data.

The claim primarily states a framework choice.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim states how the authors use the word memory inside their framework. Later assays apply that wording, but this statement itself cannot come out true or false from data. It is definitional.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The sentence stipulates a definition of memory rather than a measurable regularity. No observation would confirm or refute the decision to use that definition.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: A stipulated definition has no confirming or refuting measurement.
